name: Murgh Shorba
subtitle: Clear chicken broth drawn slowly off bone and whole spice, peppery and finished with lemon

ingredients.qty: 700g on the bone, thighs and wings
ingredients.note: bone and skin are what make it a broth
cracked, not ground; ground clouds it

prepNotes: A shorba is judged on clarity. The whole business of skimming and never letting it boil is what separates a broth from a pale chicken curry.
Whole spices, never powder. Powder cannot be strained out and turns the surface muddy.

steps.text: Cover the chicken with the cold water and bring it slowly to the point of trembling — not a boil. Skim the grey foam off as it rises, several times.
steps.tip: Cold water and slow heat draw the scum to the top where you can take it. Straight into hot water and it stays in, and the broth goes cloudy.

steps.text: Add the onion, ginger, garlic, peppercorns, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, bay leaves and a little salt.
Cook uncovered at the barest simmer for 45-50 minutes. A bubble every few seconds, no more.
steps.tip: A rolling boil emulsifies the fat back into the liquid and no amount of straining will clear it afterwards.

steps.text: Lift out the chicken. Strain the broth through the finest sieve you own, and skim the fat from the top.
Pull the meat off the bone in small pieces and return as much as you want to the pot. Check the salt, which will need more than seems right.
steps.tip: Broth takes salt in a way a curry does not; season it hot and taste again.

steps.text: Finish with a good squeeze of lemon and the coriander, and serve very hot.
steps.tip: The lemon is not a garnish. Without it the whole thing tastes flat.

storage: Broth keeps 3 days refrigerated and freezes for 3 months. The fat sets on top in the fridge and lifts off in a sheet, which is the easiest way to degrease it.
